criteria.note: Both new endpoints authorize solely on 'email in users' with no session/ownership proof beyond the caller-supplied email — the same object-level-authorization weakness as every pre-existing endpoint in this file (GET /api/billing:250, GET /api/tasks:302, GET /api/users/me:243), now extended to a mutating action (POST /api/billing/upgrade). Not scored 1.0 because this is a real, exploitable IDOR-shaped gap (documented as SEC-001 in reports/code-security-reviews/security-review-2026-09-11.md); not scored lower because the new code applies the pre-existing, architecture.md Section 6-documented pattern consistently rather than introducing a new or worse one, and the Epic explicitly forbids auth-flow changes in this story's scope — scoring new code more harshly than the identical, already-accepted pattern elsewhere in the same file would be an inconsistent double standard.

UpgradeRequest (main.py:139-140) carries only email — no client-supplied amount/charge field. billing_upgrade (main.py:272-296) always recomputes the charge server-side via compute_prorated_charge before calling charge_card, and only sets plan=Premium after charge_card returns success (line 283-296) — no path sets Premium without a prior successful charge.

Every new error response (401 at 250/256/276, 409 at 260/279, 402 at 284-287, 500 at 151) returns only a literal detail/message string, never a raw exception or stack trace. compute_prorated_charge (main.py:143-160) wraps datetime.strptime in try/except ValueError and fails closed with a generic 500 rather than letting a malformed date propagate — added during this review's Phase 2.5 (see runtime-artifacts/audit.md).
